newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Lahore bourse agrees to restructure board.
newsitem.headline: Lahore bourse agrees to restructure board.

text.p: Pakistan's Lahore Stock Exchange (LSE) said on Tuesday it would obey orders from the state Corporate Law Authority (CLA) to restructure its board of directors -- orders which the country's main Karachi bourse has vowed to resist.

"LSE has agreed to the nomination of three non-member directors on its board by the CLA and the appointment of a chief executive from outside the exchange," LSE acting president Mirza Sherdil told Reuters by telephone from Lahore.
On June 12, the CLA told the Karachi and Lahore bourses to change the composition of their boards to bring in professionals uninvolved in the equity market.
Pakistan's third Islamabad Stock Exchange already has representation of non-brokers on its board, Sherdil said.

Sherdil said the present executive post of president would be replaced by a chairman elected from the governing body of the exchange, while a chief executive would be taken from outside, with CLA approval.
The Karachi Stock Exchange has said it will resist the CLA move, which it says will compromise the bourses' independence and lead to political interference.
KSE president Arif Habib said last month the KSE would plead its case before Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz and the CLA, and could go to a court of law as the last resort.

Sherdil said board restructuring would increase investor confidence and bring more transparency. He called fears of political interference unfounded as the CLA had pledged that only professionals would be nominated to the boards.
A KSE official, who asked not to be named, said the CLA had made some changes in its earlier directives after KSE protests, but a few issues still needed to be settled.
